lines.text: The soul has escaped my body for the moment and left him on the dance floor. He can now just be
flesh and bones, rejection and heartache hit differently when there are no feelings afloat.
I want my soul now to imagine my body pulsing and head throbbing from the music and empty on
a crowded floor of sweated perfumes and temptations. Let's watch strangers collide and spark electric
currents that gamut the mood, a good one. We want him to be the last one to leave, prolonging the
bitter refraction inside the walls of an escape that few pleasures offer us. Now let us put my
soul in the middle of an open field at the equator of a planet much larger than my own
and much hotter. Cool me down by pouring unfiltered water out of the ice bath salted from the closest
moons from angels of the newest religions and its joys capturing my body transiting in a flash of
strobe lights. Their gracious cursor blessed me, only infinity will tell. Now bring my soul back
to my body to lean back, breathe in the smoke that now fills the room and tell myself how good
it is to finally get acquainted with the night, staring into unfamiliar yet relatable mountains
in the distance and wandering eyes and wandering thoughts within reach.

scenes.lines: Pulsing & head throbbing from the music— / & empty on a crowded floor of sweated perfumes & temptations.
scenes.treatment: [style: time-shifted photo-realistic] [video inspo: Madonna, Ray of Light; Janet Jackson, Got 'Til It's Gone] Leaves party/poetry-reading goes to open-air, rooftop intense club scene. Dancing is fast, lights are flashing, people are enjoying themselves, time is shifted. (p.17)

POET stands still in the middle of the moving floor, arms down; on each beat a wince — head dipping, a small crouch

bodies.action: stands still on the crowded floor, wincing on the beat

shots.action: Close on POET's face under the strobe: sweat, perfume haze drifting past, a hand touching his arm and sliding away (temptation)

bodies.action: trails a hand across his arm

scenes.lines: The soul has escaped my body for the moment / & left him on the dance floor— / He can now just be flesh & bones— / rejection & heartache hit different / when there are no feelings afloat.
scenes.treatment: Soul of POET leaves body and floats above. (p.17, beside these lines)

shots.action: The translucent soul (the same POET, glowing, see-through) peels out of his body from the same spot and rises, looking back down at him; the body sags onto one hip

bodies.action: body left behind, sags onto one hip
rises out of the body, looking back down

shots.action: Low and wide: the soul floats up above the dancers' raised hands into the open sky over the rooftop
From the soul's height, looking down: the body standing alone in the moving crowd, just flesh and bones; small dark weights fall and settle at his feet instead of rising

scenes.lines: I want my soul now to imagine my body. / Let's watch strangers collide & spark electric currents that gamut the mood— a good one. / We want him to be the last one to leave, / prolonging the bitter refraction from the escape— / inside the walls of an escape that few pleasures offer us.
scenes.treatment: Cut away to POET's Soul watching party floating from afar, top-down of all Atlantis, lit up, blue and pink lights throughout the city. (p.18, beside 'bitter refraction from the escape— inside the walls of an escape')

shots.action: Two strangers on the floor reach for each other and collide; a visible spark of electric current jumps between them and spreads colour through the crowd

bodies.action: reaches and collides with a stranger
sways loosely behind them, arms swinging

shots.action: Cut away: top-down from far above, all of Atlantis lit up blue and pink; the soul floats small in the foreground, watching the rooftop party glow

bodies.action: floats high above the city, watching

shots.action: The floor thins; the body is still dancing slowly, the last one left

bodies.action: keeps dancing slowly as others leave

scenes.lines: Now let us put my soul in the middle of an open field— / at the equator of a planet much larger than my own— / & much hotter.
scenes.treatment: No note on the planet itself; staged from the line. The treatment's next note sits beside these lines (p.18): 'Cut back to body in club, angels dumping cleansing water on POET's Body in the middle of the club scene.' — set up here, paid off in 08.5.

shots.action: The soul stands alone in the middle of an endless flat plain on a planet so big its curve barely shows; equator markers run across the ground; a huge white sun
The glare burns the air out of the sky; the soul shields its eyes, head turned away

bodies.action: shields its eyes from the sun

shots.action: Cut back: the body on the club floor, sweating, overheated; above it, angels appear in the haze

bodies.action: appears above him in the haze

scenes.lines: Cool me down by pouring unfiltered water / out of ice baths—salted from the closest moons / from angles of the newest religions / & its joys capturing my body trancing in a flash of strobe lights. / their graces curse or bless me— / only infinity will tell.
scenes.treatment: Cut back to body in club, angels dumping cleansing water on POET's Body in the middle of the club scene. (p.18)

shots.action: In the middle of the club, three angels, hovering at different angles, tip ice-bath basins and pour cold water over the POET's body; the dancers keep dancing around him

bodies.action: takes the water, flinching, arms opening
pours a basin from the left
pours a basin from the right

shots.action: Close on the body under the strobe as the water hits: head back, eyes shut, moon-salt crystals glittering on his skin
Intercut: on the hot plain the soul unbends as the cold reaches it; a pool spreads round its feet, salt piling at the edges, steam leaving

scenes.lines: Now bring my soul back to my body / to lean back— / breathe in the smoke that now fills the room— / & tell myself how good it is to finally get acquainted with the night.
scenes.treatment: Club fills with haze, POET's Body inhales it as POET's soul returns. (p.19)

shots.action: Haze rolls across the club floor and fills it; the soul glides down along the path it left by
The body leans back and breathes the smoke in deep; the soul settles into him and its glow sinks under his skin

bodies.action: leans back and inhales the haze

shots.action: 'how good it is to finally get acquainted with the night': POET smiles slightly, eyes open on the night sky

bodies.action: looks up at the night, at ease

scenes.lines: Staring into unfamiliar yet—relatable mountains in the distance / & wandering eyes & wandering thoughts within reach. / [Yet, Heard:] accepting you'll never say nor ever feel my love was real— / what isn't mine, I still can not give.
scenes.treatment: POET stares into mountains from rooftop. (p.19) Then, no voice over [inspo video: Juice Jones, The Rain]: POET leaves clubs, walks down street. Crowds on the sidewalk, as men and woman fawn over POET. POET sees EX through crowd (still back of EX, no face shown) and tries to reach him but cannot. (p.19; the last two lines are printed under Yet, Heard but belong to this movement in the world module)

shots.action: POET sits on the rooftop ledge, his back to the club, staring at a mountain range beyond the city, pale under a second, almost identical range

bodies.action: sits on the ledge staring at the mountains

shots.action: No voiceover. POET walks down the night street out of the club; men and women on the sidewalk turn to him, reach for his arm, call to him

bodies.action: walks down the sidewalk, not stopping

shots.action: POET's view through the crowd: the EX, back to us, walking away further down the street
POET pushes through the crowd and reaches out toward the EX, but bodies close between them and the EX is gone

bodies.action: reaches out through the crowd, cannot get through

passage.line: The soul has escaped my body for the moment and left him on the dance floor. He can now just be
passage.why_fulcrum: The poem's whole idea in one line: the soul steps out and the body is left behind on the dance floor, alone among people. Everything after it is told from outside himself.

answer.title: Beginning to Date
answer.said: Crossing that wide dance floor and asking a girl to dance can seem frightening,
answer.why: A 1953 school film on manners describes the same floor as something to cross, a fear to get over. He is already out on it, and his soul has gone.

passage.gesture_detail: He stands with his arms loose and his body sways a little to a beat he no longer feels; his head lowers to the floor, where the answer opens.
passage.surface: floor: the wet, polished floor under string lights, which reflects

plate.why: Naraka Market's string lights and crowded twilight make the club's outside; its wet street floor reflects them like a dance floor.

passage.staging: POET in the middle of the lit floor; string lights above; the archive opens in the reflection at his feet.
